weak.title: Weak scaling, blast lattice L, subcycled (single MFC build, 2 reps)
weak.note: Same physics, grid and dt. MFC: one case-optimized build (651b6d88), 5-equation single fluid, mp_weno off, AMReX tag rule, 2 reps (sd <= 0.01 s/step), without owner placement. Weak-scaling efficiency np8 -> np512: MFC 0.72, AMReX 0.69, PeleC 0.63 (subcycled); lock-step MFC 0.96 vs AMReX 0.68. MFC np128/np512 subcycled from 239-step runs (the step-240 regrid ran out of GPU memory; being fixed). MFC refines more volume (40.5% vs 30.3%). Owner placement (merged, opt-in) took np64 subcycled from 2.07 to 1.38 s/step in tests; ladder rerun on the integrated build pending.

conv.title: MFC: subcycled minus lock-step solution vs level-0 dt
conv.note: Plotted: max difference between subcycled and lock-step solutions (not error vs exact). Conservation: subcycled runs within 1.5e-15, lock-step two-level runs within 7.9e-15 (roundoff); 1 and 4 ranks bit-identical. Quartic prolongation (amr_prolong = 2) makes subcycling second order; with regrid, new fine cells must also be seeded with the quartic (fix found by diffing against the mini-app).

cov.title: Refined share of the domain at matched time
cov.note: Coverage of the grid actually used in the last timed steps (regrid after step 220) for every code. MFC required same-level blocks to meet face to face, so each blast became one bounding cube; the new opt-in tile clustering brings MFC to AMReX's refined volume (15.3% vs 15.45%, 29.6% vs 30.25%), currently 4x slower per step until its per-block work is batched.

phase.title: Where MFC's time goes, blast L, 8 GPUs
phase.note: Fill and halo = gather + gfill + halo + seam. Other = swap + rk. Level-0 RHS alone is 80 ms per stage for 8M cells per GPU; the mini-app's whole non-subcycled step is 95 ms.

convm.title: Mini-app: the same test, minmod vs quartic
convm.note: The C/HIP reference implementation found the prolongation limit first (finding F1) and predicted the quartic fix that MFC now confirms.

amr.title: AMR-only cost per coarse step (everything except each code's own hydro RHS), single MFC build
amr.note: Lock-step MFC AMR cost is flat 8->128 GPUs. Subcycled MFC AMR cost is the outlier (0.6 -> 1.13 s/step); the targets being fixed are regrid storage and migration, owner-aware placement, the subcycling driver, per-block batching and RHS host syncs. No adjustment of MFC's RHS timer is applied here.

status.title: Ready to show
items: Flagship movie: Mach 2.5 shock through a curtain of 64 free spheres, 80 GPUs, volumetric shocks, vortex wakes, GPU-coloured cutaway with callouts, plus three 4K hero stills: curtain movie and stills. Second example: 8-sphere movie.

Subcycling in MFC: one and two refined levels, conservative to ~1e-15, bit-identical across ranks, second order with quartic prolongation (also with regrid). Quartic interfaces match a uniform fine grid; minmod is 10^4-10^5x worse (figure below). Full GPU regression suite 789/789.

Weak scaling to 512 GPUs vs AMReX and PeleC (single MFC build, 2 reps, audited): total-time efficiency 8->512 GPUs, subcycled MFC 0.72 vs AMReX 0.69 vs PeleC 0.63; lock-step MFC 0.96 vs AMReX 0.68. MFC is 2-3x slower in absolute time (heavier RHS, more refined volume).
Where the time goes: AMR-only cost by category, RHS profile, OpenMP vs HIP (MFC's RHS cost is its own code, not the programming model).
Reference mini-app: 2.6-4.5x faster per step than AMReX/PeleC at 512 GPUs, 0.95-0.96 weak-scaling efficiency with owner placement; its findings drove the MFC fixes.

Found and fixed, with evidence: reflux race (multi-rank nondeterminism), snap crash, first-order subcycling from minmod seeding, regrid out-of-memory at 128 GPUs, coverage matched to AMReX with tile clustering.

status.title: MFC before vs after (integrated build, 8-128 GPUs in)
items: Subcycled s/step 1.574/1.953/2.020 -> 0.765/0.797/0.833 at 8/64/128 GPUs (2.0-2.4x faster); lock-step 0.478/0.455/0.464 -> 0.251/0.261/0.263. np128 subcycled now runs all 240 steps (v1 ran out of memory at the last regrid).
Weak scaling 8->128 GPUs: MFC subcycled +9% vs AMReX +31%, PeleC +39%; lock-step MFC +5% vs AMReX +33%. MFC now matches PeleC per step at 64-128 GPUs; AMReX still ~1.35x faster subcycled.
AMR-only s/step now below AMReX in both modes and below PeleC at 64-128 GPUs (subcycled 0.217/0.233/0.260). Owner placement accounts for 24% of the np64 subcycled step (1.052 off vs 0.797 on).
Pending: 512-GPU reps (queued for this afternoon/evening), final validation round on the integrated branch, then push.
